headline: Joel Embiid, LeBron James lead Eastern Conference-leading 76ers past the Bucks 132-129
text: PHILADELPHIA -- — Joel Embiid had 26 points and 17 rebounds, LeBron James scored 13 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers held on for a 132-129 victory over Tyler Herro and the last-place Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Herro scored a career-high 50 points and nearly sent the game into overtime for Milwaukee, which lost its 13th in a row and 16th in 17 contests to start the season. Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists. Tyrese Maxey added 17 points for the 76ers (14-3), who won their fifth straight. Jaylen Brown did not play for the second consecutive contest because of a hamstring strain. Philadelphia looked in complete control, up 10 with just over two minutes left, before a furious comeback attempt by the Bucks. Herro's layup with 19.2 seconds remaining pulled Milwaukee within 128-126. After a pair of free throws by Embiid, Brayden Burries drained a corner 3-pointer with 4.8 seconds left to make it 130-129. Embiid then made two free throws with 1.5 seconds to play to put Philadelphia up by three. Herro's shot to tie from the right wing went in, but he released it after the buzzer. After a sluggish first half in which they trailed by as many as seven points, the 76ers came to life in the third quarter with the help of James. He got the crowd roaring with a dunk early in the period, blocked Kyle Kuzma and then passed to Maxey for a driving layup that put Philadelphia ahead for good, 71-70 with just over seven minutes left in the period. Anfernee Simons helped Philadelphia extend its lead to double-digits with eight straight points during the quarter. Dean Wade (hamstring) and Adem Bona (neck) also were sidelined for the 76ers. Dominick Barlow tallied 12 points for Philadelphia in his first appearance after missing the first 16 games with a lower back injury. Ousmane Dieng had successful surgery on his left finger fracture and is expected to return in the “near term,” Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins said before the game. Herro made 15 of 23 field goals, including 7 of 12 3-pointers, while eclipsing his previous best scoring game of 41 points. Up next Bucks: At Toronto on Monday. 76ers: Host Portland on Monday. ------ This story has been corrected to show the 76ers next host Portland on Monday, not Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Brunson scores 30, Bridges hits 3 at buzzer, lifting Knicks to 97-96 win over Trail Blazers
text: NEW YORK -- — Jalen Brunson scored 30 points, Mikel Bridges hit the winning 3-pointer at the buzzer, and the New York Knicks edged the Portland Trail Blazers 97-96 on Saturday night. The defending champions led by 26 points in the first half before Portland charged back and took a 96-94 lead with 3.4 seconds left after a pair of free throws from Deni Avdija . New York called a timeout to advance the ball past half court and Josh Hart found Bridges on the wing as Toumani Camara leapt past him. Bridges calmly hit his second 3-pointer of the night before he was mobbed by his teammates. Brunson scored 19 of his 30 points in the first quarter and Landry Shamet had 20 for the Knicks, who won their fourth consecutive game on a night they honored 50 alumni. Donovan Clingan finished with 22 points and 13 rebounds, and Avdija had 20 for Portland, who have lost three of their last four games — all on the road. The Knicks led 66-43 at the break — the fewest points they have allowed in the first half this season — before Portland mounted its rally. The Trail Blazers — whose 43 points over the first two quarters were a season low — outscored New York 29-15 in the third period and cut the deficit to six points with 58 seconds remaining in the quarter before Shamet’s 3-pointer extended the Knicks lead to 81-72. Portland fell behind by 13 after a 3-point play from Tyler Kolek extended the New York lead 92-79. Camara and Lillard scored consecutive baskets before Jose Alvarado’s layup made it 94-84. Lillard then sparked a 12-0 run capped by Advija’s free throws after he was fouled by Andre Drummond , who attempted to strip the ball away, before Bridges’ last-second 3. Up Next Trail Blazers: Visit Philadelphia on Monday night. Knicks: Host Indiana on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Kyrie Irving scores 25, Cooper Flagg 22 as the Mavericks top the Clippers 110-100
text: DALLAS -- — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night. Walter Clayton Jr . added 16 points and Max Christie finished with 13, both off the bench, as Dallas (9-7) began a back-to-back with a second consecutive win at home following an 0-3 trip. Brook Lopez scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half to lead the Clippers (4-11), who have dropped three straight overall and are 0-7 on the road. Rui Hachimura had 19 points, matching a season high with four 3-pointers. After the Clippers’ Kris Dunn hit a corner 3 that cut Dallas’ lead to 91-88 with 5:12 left, the Mavericks scored 11 in a row aided by two Los Angeles turnovers. Irving opened shooting 1 of 7 from the floor but scored 12 points in the fourth quarter. Flagg went 7 of 13 at the foul line, the first time last season’s NBA Rookie of the Year — an 84.2% free-throw shooter — has missed six in his brief career. Clayton and Christie combined to go 5 of 7 from behind the arc. The Clippers entered last in the NBA in rebounding, averaging 39 per game. They beat the Mavericks on the boards 54-52 but were outscored 20-19 in second-chance points. The Mavericks played their first game this season without starting forward P.J. Washington Jr., who sat out with an illness. Up next Clippers: Visit Houston on Monday. Mavericks: At Utah on Sunday night to begin a three-game trip. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jaden McDaniels scores 25 and Timberwolves top short-handed Grizzlies 104-95
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points, Ayo Dosunmu added 19 and the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the short-handed Memphis Grizzlies 104-95 on Saturday night. Jonathan Kuminga scored 16 points, Terrence Shannon Jr . added 15 and LaMelo Ball had 12 as Minnesota shot a season-high 58% from the field. Minnesota has won three of four; however, it continues searching for consistent offensive flow without injured Anthony Edwards . The Timberwolves had 23 turnovers after having 17 and 21 in its prior two games. Cedric Coward tied a season high with 23 points to lead Memphis, which lost for the first time in six games and first time on the road in nine starts. The Grizzlies have the league’s top offensive rating, but recorded season lows in points in a quarter (12), half (46) and game against the league’s top defensive rated team. Memphis played without power forward Cam Boozer (right ankle sprain), second on the team with 16.6 points per game to go along with a team-high 9.2 rebounds, and forward Jerami Grant (left calf strain). Coach Tuomas Iisalo said pregame that Boozer was undergoing further evaluations and “there will be a medical update later on” regarding Grant. Guard Ty Jerome , averaging a team-high 25.4 points, scored 18 in his first game back after missing four games with a right hip impingement. Down by 23 points early in the fourth quarter, Memphis got within 97-90 with 2:37 left, but McDaniels countered with back-to-back layups for Minnesota. Minnesota outscored Memphis 28-12 in the second quarter to take control. Down by 11 early in the frame, the Timberwolves went on a 26-6 run capped by a Rudy Gobert dunk off a missed Ball free throw on their way to a 56-46 lead at the break. Dosunmu had three driving layups as the Timberwolves scored 14 of the final 16 points of the third quarter for an 83-62 advantage. Up next Grizzlies: At Charlotte on Monday. Timberwolves: Host Brooklyn on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Victor Wembanyama has 50 points, 19 rebounds on dominant night as Spurs roll past Pelicans, 114-91
text: SAN ANTONIO -- — Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, with 32 coming in the first half, along with 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs rolled to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday. Wembanyama is the first player with 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game this season and he did so by halftime. Stephon Castle added 19 points, six assists and three rebounds for San Antonio, which has won 14 of 15 to join the Los Angeles Lakers atop the Western Conference at 14-3. Jeremiah Fears had 29 points and Jordan Poole added 25 points in New Orleans' third consecutive loss. Wembanyama exited shortly after reaching 50 points on a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 remaining in the game. He finished two points shy of the career high he set Nov. 4 against Dallas. Dylan Harper missed his second straight game with a strained left hip suffered on Tuesday against Detroit in San Antonio’s lone loss since Oct. 23. The Spurs limited their turnovers to 13 after committing a season-high 21 in their first game without Harper. San Antonio outscored New Orleans 82-62 over the final three quarters. The Spurs captured a 61-45 lead at halftime after two scuffles in the second quarter. Jaron Pierre Jr . shoved Wembanyama from behind after the 7-foot-4 center was fouled by Karlo Matković with 9:27 remaining in the first half. Technical fouls were given to Pierre and Keldon Johnson , who confronted the Pelicans forward after the shove. Wembanyama responded by scoring the next seven points, including spinning around Yves Missi for a one-handed slam. De'Aaron Fox received a technical and had to be separated with 3:49 remaining in the first half after the Spurs guard gave a two-handed shove to Fears following a backcourt violation on the New Orleans guard. Wembanyama again responded, scoring the next five points. New Orleans was without Zion Williamson (bruised left thigh), Trey Murphy III (knee) and Bennedict Mathurin (left plantar fasciitis). Former Spurs point guard Dejounte Murray remains away from the Pelicans after having his agent, Rich Paul, request a trade from New Orleans on Nov. 13. Up next Pelicans: Host Phoenix on Monday. Spurs: At Sacramento on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Murray's putback with 5 seconds left lifts Kings to 97-96 win over Celtics, ending 8-game skid
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Keegan Murray 's putback over three defenders with 5 seconds left lifted the Sacramento Kings to a 97-96 victory over the Boston Celtics on Saturday night. The Kings snapped an eight-game losing streak and earned their first home win this season following a back-and-forth game down the stretch. Trailing by one with 11.8 seconds left, Darius Acuff Jr . drove the lane and his shot was off. Murray grabbed the putback and scored to give the Kings a one-point advantage. Payton Pritchard had a chance to win it for Boston at the buzzer, but his 20-footer was off. All five Kings starters scored in double figures, led by Acuff's 21 points, eight assists and six rebounds. Murray added 15 points and 12 rebounds. Jayson Tatum (rest), Derrick White (shoulder) and Mitchell Robinson (illness) did not play against Sacramento, leaving Boston undermanned. The Celtics' defense smothered the Kings early on, forcing multiple turnovers and vaulting Boston to a 10-0 lead. Sacramento went into halftime down 54-41. But the Kings' defense, which ranks near the bottom of the NBA in opponents points per game at 120.7, held the Celtics well below that. A 35-13 third quarter in favor of Sacramento turned the game, as Boston missed all 13 of its 3-point attempts in the period. The Celtics took 58 3-pointers overall and made only 22%. Sacramento took a 76-67 lead into the fourth, but the Celtics fought back. Pritchard hit a step-back shot to put them up 96-95 with 11.8 seconds to go. Paul George scored 19 points to lead Boston. Up next Celtics: Visit Golden State on Sunday. Kings: Host San Antonio on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
